core.title: Keep design-system files from importing application or slice code
core.given: A file under a design root (the stack's shared, consumer-agnostic design asset tree, whose first-level subdirectories name its layers; which directories are design roots and what those layers are called come from the profile)
core.when: it references another module in the repository by a relative path
core.then: The import MUST NOT resolve outside the file's containing design root; the design system stays independent of the application and slice code that consumes it.
prefer: Pass application-specific values into design components as inputs, or move genuinely shared, design-owned types or constants inward.
During GREEN: satisfy the current value through component inputs or existing design-system contracts.
During GREEN: add only the smallest input surface the acceptance requires.
During GREEN: move a type or constant only when it is truly owned by the design system.
avoid: Importing slice code through a barrel or an alias.
Relocating application-specific concepts into design code just to make the import legal.
Broadening the fix by generalizing unrelated design APIs.
unless: Test files and vendored or build trees are never scanned.
References to modules outside the project graph (external packages) are not judged.
Aliased references are judged only when the alias names a design root.
A repository with no design root is not judged: there is no shared design system to connect to yet.
core.why: Application and slice code import FROM the design system, never the reverse, keeping it slice-agnostic; a system that reaches into a slice becomes part of it, cannot be reused by the next slice, and breaks when that slice changes.
evidence: The design-root import check reports no outward import for any file under a design root.
Design-system files import nothing from application or slice code.
The current behavioral or rendering acceptance passes.
verification: Disposition strict: violations are enforced, not waived (severity 3 in the reference realization).

Scope: the check covers every file under a design root and every relative in-project reference in it, existing or newly added; a detector that scans only some file kinds has a coverage limit, not a narrower rule.

Boundary enforced is the containing design root: a relative reference that leaves the importing file's design root is outward even when it lands inside another design root (the stricter statement wording is kept; cross-root references are not exempt).
Aliased references are resolved and judged only when the alias names a design root; alias-resolution mechanics belong to the realization.

Never scanned: test files (the stack's test-file name patterns, an undifferentiated set the stack does not split by unit/acceptance/e2e kind) and vendored/build trees (the exact trees are the stack-wide excluded-roots list, owned by the profile/checker).
References to modules outside the project graph are not judged.
Self-scoping: a repository with no design root is not judged.

fires: A file under a design root adds a relative reference that resolves outside the design root, into application or slice code.
A file under a design root already contains (unchanged) a relative reference that resolves into application or slice code.
A design-owned source file under a design root imports a type or constant from a slice via a relative path.
A design-root file references through an alias that names a design root but resolves to application or slice code.
A file under one design root references a relative path that leaves its containing design root (the containing-root boundary is enforced; cross-design-root references are not exempt).
doesNotFire: The repository has no design root.
Application or slice code imports from the design system (the allowed direction).
A design-root file references an external package outside the project graph.
A test file or a file in a vendored/build tree under the design root references outward.
A design-root file uses an alias that does not name a design root.
A relative reference whose target stays inside the importing file's own design root.

profileRequirements.meaning: Which directories constitute a design root: the shared, consumer-agnostic design asset tree that application and slice code may import from but that must not reach back out. Needed for the given, the activation fact and the boundary the check enforces.

The layer directories directly beneath a design root: the first directory under a design root names the design layer a file belongs to. Locating context inside the design tree; the obligation itself does not depend on it.
profileRequirements.bunValue: tokens or foundations, primitives, components, templates

profileRequirements.meaning: Name patterns that identify a test file of any kind; files matching them under a design root are never scanned. The reference stack excludes test naming as one undifferentiated set, not split by unit, acceptance or end-to-end kind.
Vendored and generated/build trees that are never scanned; one stack-wide list whose exact classification is owned by the profile/checker (the rule text defers the exact trees).
How a reference to an external package (outside the project graph) is recognised, so that such references are excluded from judgement.

proposedKeys.meaning: Directory names/globs that constitute a design root: the shared, consumer-agnostic design asset tree that application and slice code imports from but that must not reach back out.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The roles group covers only the ten architectural/artifact roles; a design system is a cross-slice shared asset tree, not one of them, and layout.commons_dir describes code shared across features within the product rather than a consumer-agnostic design tree. roles.<role>.path cannot express it because 'design system' is not an allowed role parameter.

proposedKeys.meaning: The layer directories directly beneath a design root; the first directory under a design root names the design layer a file belongs to.
proposedKeys.bunValue: tokens or foundations, primitives, components, templates
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roles.layers lists the stack's architectural layer roles (e.g. presentation, application, domain, integration); the design tree's internal layers are a directory-shape fact inside the design root, and no existing layout key describes the design root's internal structure.

proposedKeys.meaning: Name patterns that identify a test file of any kind, for stacks whose test-file naming does not distinguish unit, acceptance and end-to-end tests.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: suffix.<file_kind> is parametric only over unit_test, acceptance_test and e2e_test separately; this rule's source excludes one undifferentiated set of test-file patterns, so assigning it to a single kind changes that key's meaning, and assigning it to all three kinds asserts distinctions the source does not make.

neutralityNotes: The 'design root' concept has no closed profile key, so layout.design_root is proposed; without it no stack could instantiate the given or the boundary. The design tree's internal layering is preserved neutrally in the core's given (the first directory beneath a design root names the layer), with the concrete layer names supplied through the proposed layout.design_layers key rather than stranded as Bun-only. 'Wagon' is rendered as 'slice' (a bounded product slice); the core needs no wagon-location key because the obligation is stated purely as the containing-design-root boundary, under which application and slice code both fall. The Bun test-file exclusion names *.test.* and *.spec.* as one undifferentiated set; no closed key covers aggregate test-file naming (suffix.unit_test names unit-test files only), so the aggregate suffix.test key is proposed instead of redefining a per-kind key. Alias-resolution mechanics and the detector's file-kind coverage list (.tsx/.jsx/.html/.css) stay realization-side: the core records only that aliases naming a design root are judged and that limited detector coverage is not a narrowing. The containing-root vs every-root source tension is preserved in core:verification exactly as the rewrite resolves it (stricter containing-root boundary, cross-root imports not exempt).
